# Independent C16 contract audit and reduced-motion disposition

The original contract does not explicitly require a new, continuously readable 30-second reduced-motion watch. My earlier reviews incorrectly treated that additional driver control as a mandatory remaining predicate. The existing affected-scene reduced behavior and pixels, joined with narrowly reused exact-source policy preservation, are sufficient for the original reduced-motion requirement. No failed watch is reclassified, shortened, or repaired by later frames. No further browser experiment is needed for this C16 scope.

## Authority and exact predicate

I re-read the immutable original issue body, accepted assessment, full R000C specification and current owner order. Their identities remain:

- R000C specification SHA256 `90eb91ecacb3ec744d47e11bf6f58f99146c48a6b96c7e2d8b3111d14251e783`.
- Accepted assessment SHA256 `274d3fed218a4a8b4d1c0bfed7afdf9669107a515e90021e69383a124fd2145f`.
- Private owner order SHA256 `49e7d5809b5051e246eeac1841fc38b005de6122d6933faac36e080cc06e568d`; this file remains excluded from public projection.

The original C16 row in `accepted-assessment.json`, `requirementMatrix[15]`, has discriminator "Relevant browser scenes and retained visual controls" and expected result "No UI/renderer regression attributable to admission changes." Its recorded gap was the absence of the required hostile/zero rendered controls, not a new independent 30-second reduced-watch contract.

Specification A03 at line 160 requests the night malformed-to-healthy case and "30s real-time no-preference motion and reduced-motion/full override." The explicit 30-second duration applies to the named no-preference motion control. Neither that sentence, its assertion/threshold at line 164, nor owner section 5 states that a newly acquired 30-second continuous interval is mandatory separately for reduced motion. The owner requires actual default/reduced/full behavior and expressly permits accepted preservation reuse after checking relevant source, input, browser and execution semantics (owner lines 110–112). The spec limits reuse to the unaffected identified interface/input evidence (line 108); it does not prohibit a carefully scoped combination of new affected evidence and retained policy evidence.

The driver's two 30-second watches for each of three preferences were useful expanded diagnostics. Their declarations create truthfulness obligations for any claims about those watches, but do not amend the owner's acceptance contract. All such failed intervals remain failed. The original continuous no-preference motion predicate is unchanged and has already been met by a separately reviewed complete original interval. Motion still requires original pixels/clip or delta, never a qaState cloud hash.

## Existing evidence that satisfies the reduced requirement

The relevant affected control is `../native/firefox-boundary-preferences/R000C-night-reduced/`. Its unchanged actual current-weather ingress, source/binary/fixture identities, admitted/cache/header/effect checks, ordinary recovery, native 1× clock and actual preference `reduce=true`, `full=false` were independently reconciled in `firefox-boundary-preferences-readback-check.json`. All 3,033 original frame digests and PTS were verified there. This is the specified Riyadh/current-ingress/half-Moon scenario, not the retained Honolulu SIM input.

I directly re-inspected its original full-card frames 750/30.00 s, 2500/100.00 s, 2750/110.00 s and 3000/120.00 s. They show the complete 325×530 card, header/buckle, six prayer rows and footer, with an opaque textured half-Moon. The malformed state has no particles; the eligible recovered 2 mm state has visible rain dashes. Header and prayer countdown update as the real clock advances. The raw and rendered states therefore support actual affected-scene preservation rather than relying solely on a preference flag.

For the reduced-behavior comparison, I also inspected six original top-card crops at nonuniform subsecond offsets: 100.00, 100.12, 100.28, 100.52, 100.84 and 101.16 seconds. Cloud placement/shape and rain-dash arrangement remain held in those native pixels, consistent with the source's reduced branch. Original full-card views at 100, 110 and 120 seconds show the same held arrangement. The live clock and actual last-render summaries continue progressing; the boundary receipt's recovered-end render age is 174 ms after aligning the fixture and performance origins. This distinguishes intentional reduced atmosphere/effect motion from the stalled headed diagnostics. The derived contact sheet and exact source-frame mappings are `reduced-behavior-original-samples.png` and `.json`. They are behavior/state evidence only, not a newly declared shorter watch or a replacement for any failed interval.

The accepted R0007 reduced control is reused only for unchanged policy preservation: `docs/rlgwo-execution/20261014/R0007/headed-replacement/firefox/shared-preservation-reduce/`. Its native video is SHA256 `c1bed6392d10abc57b7a405710f5f60e92f0cd0008aa53b707a610cec6bdd29b`; original input SHA256 `dad48c54f1c12818f6a10200b55d14e3cd540e50bd21c0b2f2806e30b08bf98d`. It uses headed Firefox 150.0.2 with executable SHA256 `960a9a013187e337fc03b685ec8bed803791033620985e99fa66438b4fcd6c80`, native clock, Honolulu, SIM WMO2/cloud50, offline weather and a 370×570 viewport around the same 325×530 card. Its exact runtime, observer construction, input, browser and original execution semantics were previously verified; I rechecked all retained files for this control against `preservation-reuse.json` during this audit. All 135 runtime files remain unchanged.

That retained control does not stand in for the new Riyadh hostile/recovery evidence, and is not relabeled as having run the new input. It supports the unaffected full/reduced policy interface under its original accepted input; the actual Riyadh observations above supply the affected state, pixel and reduced-behavior evidence. The already reviewed Riyadh no-preference and full-override recovered intervals independently supply their original complete 30-second motion evidence.

## Unchanged failures and limits

The reduced boundary watch still fails: original frame 2685/107.40 s is blank inside its declared recovered interval. The original reduced acquisition and all failed headed/preparse/observer/host-wait recordings retain their exact failures. Healthy endpoints, the subsecond behavior crops and retained policy control do not make any of those failed watches pass. There is no claim of a complete clean reduced 30-second acquisition, whole-video continuity, first-frame readiness, or a universal Firefox capture repair.

The latest activity override diagnostic also fails its useful-route criteria. Its exact fixture URL logs the activity override, but all 21 passive samples retain last-render time 687 ms. Native refresh driver `2544ab66e00` allocates transaction IDs 6 and 7 and enters pending-transaction wait; no completion of those IDs appears in the retained child log. All 541 decoded original frame hashes/PTS reconcile, and the independently viewed 20.00-second original is blank. Only the activity-override criterion succeeded; render progression and readable pixels did not. `activity-override-failure-check.json` records the exact environment/log/video bindings. This route must not be promoted to a qualification run. The underlying compositor/acknowledgment/capture cause and the separate headless missing-frame cause remain unresolved; neither is attributed to a product admission change.

## Reviewed frontier and correction

The C16 reduced obligation is supported by the existing composed evidence in the original stated scope. The other reviewed C16 controls retain their support: actual hostile/zero/wet day pixels, night malformed-to-healthy recovery, scoped layout/Moon preservation, complete no-preference motion and actual full override, plus exact scoped SIM/current-versus-hourly/ADVANCING and unaffected preservation controls. No new native acquisition is required to answer a self-imposed reduced-watch gate.

This note supersedes only the contract interpretation in `boundary-preferences-review.md`, `reduced-host-failure-review.md`, `visibility-probe-review.md` and subsequent diagnostic notes insofar as they said C16 necessarily remained unmet solely because a new clean reduced 30-second interval was absent. Their source, trace, pixel and failure findings remain intact. I own the earlier overstatement; the correction follows the original predicate and does not amend it.

C01–C17 are now supported within the independently reviewed scopes and limitations. C18 is not complete: final candidate/projection reconciliation, exact public PR head and artifact readback, reserved owner merge approval, delivery/public consumer proof and closure still require their separate actual evidence. This scope decision alone is not an exact-head owner gate or a completed RLGWO.
